chunks: It is narrated from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who gives another man his land, in which there is water, palm trees, and fruit, and says: “Water this from the water and cultivate it, and you shall have half of what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, brings forth from it.” He said: “There is no harm in it.”

He said: I also asked him about a man who gives another man ruined land and says: “Develop it, and it is yours for three years, or four, or five years, or whatever he wishes.” He said: “There is no harm in that.”

He said: I further asked him about a man who owns land from the kharaj lands, upon which there is a known tax that may sometimes increase and sometimes decrease, and he gives it to another man on the condition that he cover its tax and give him two hundred dirhams in the year. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَرْضَهُ: his land; the property being given for cultivation or use
key_terms.اعْمُرْهُ: cultivate or develop it; make the land productive
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ الْخَرِبَةَ: ruined land; uncultivated or undeveloped land
key_terms.الْخَرَاجِ: kharaj; land tax imposed on certain lands
key_terms.خَرَاجٌ مَعْلُومٌ: a known tax; a specified kharaj obligation
key_terms.مَاءٌ: water; the irrigation source present on the land
key_terms.مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ: two hundred dirhams; the stated annual payment
key_terms.نَخْلٌ: palm trees; part of the productive assets on the land

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to lease or cultivate land on a profit-sharing or tax-covering arrangement?
ai.summary: This hadith states the permissibility of several land-use arrangements, including profit-sharing cultivation, temporary development of ruined land, and transferring use of kharaj land in exchange for covering its tax and paying a fixed amount. It reflects jurisprudential allowance in agricultural and financial dealings when such terms are agreed upon.
